title: Q&A: How do MCA factor rates work and what do they cost?
section_heading: Q: i got offered a 50k mca with a 1.4 factor rate how much am i really paying is this a good deal or am i getting ripped off
chunk_text: A: The factor rate of 1.4 means you'll pay a fee of $14,000 on a $10,000 advance. This translates to an extremely high equivalent APR, but the exact APR should be discussed as it depends on the repayment period and method. To get a better understanding of the deal, I recommend calling 1-800-889-0232.

title: Q&A: How do MCA factor rates work and what do they cost?
section_heading: Q: they gave me twenty five grand and said the factor rate was 1.29 and now they want thirty two grand back in like six months this is way more than i thought is that normal or am i just stupid for signing it
chunk_text: A: The factor rate of 1.29 is applied directly to the principal advance amount of $25,000. This means the total repayment amount is $31,750 ($25,000 x 1.29), which is higher than the $32,000 you mentioned. Paying off the advance early does not reduce the fee, which is a characteristic of merchant cash advances.

title: Q&A: How do MCA factor rates work and what do they cost?
section_heading: Q: my friend said factor rates are a total scam how much does a 1.49 factor rate really cost me on a 75k loan
chunk_text: A: If a business receives a $75,000 advance with a factor rate of 1.49, the total repayment amount would be $75,000 x 1.49. This means the fee would be $112,250 - $75,000 = $37,250.

title: Q&A: What should a business owner do when juggling multiple simultaneous MCAs they can't keep up with?
section_heading: Q: 4 mcas crushing my business like 60 grand total please help me
chunk_text: A: The total repayment amount for a $25,000 merchant cash advance with a factor rate of 1.29 is $31,750. This is calculated by multiplying the principal advance amount by the factor rate. Paying off the advance early does not reduce the fee.
